back_translation: Behold, a day is coming for the LORD, when your plunder will be divided in your midst.

“For I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle, and the city will be captured, the houses plundered, and the women violated. Half of the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.”
Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations, as He fights on a day of battle.

On that day His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, which lies east of Jerusalem, and the Mount of Olives will be split in two from east to west, forming a very great valley; half the mountain will move to the north and half to the south.

You will flee by the valley of My mountains, for the valley will reach to Azal. You will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with Him.
On that day there will be no light; the luminaries will grow dim.
It will be a unique day, known to the LORD, neither day nor night; but when evening comes, there will be light.
On that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half of it toward the eastern sea and half toward the western sea, in summer and in winter alike.
And the LORD will be King over all the earth; on that day the LORD will be one, and His name one.

All the land will be turned into a plain, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem; but Jerusalem will be raised up and remain in her place, from the Benjamin Gate to the place of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the royal winepresses.
People will dwell in it, and there will be no more curse of destruction; Jerusalem will dwell in security.

This will be the plague with which the LORD strikes all the peoples who waged war against Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they stand on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.
On that day a great panic from the LORD will fall upon them, so that each will seize the hand of another, and the hand of one will rise against the hand of another.
Judah also will fight at Jerusalem, and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered—gold, silver, and garments in great abundance.
A similar plague will strike the horse, the mule, the camel, the donkey, and all the animals in those camps, like this plague.
Then all who survive of the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, and to keep the Feast of Booths.
And if any of the families of the earth do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, no rain will fall on them.

And if the family of Egypt does not go up and take part, no rain will fall on them either; this will be the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations that do not go up to keep the Feast of Booths.
This will be the punishment of Egypt and the punishment of all the nations that do not go up to keep the Feast of Booths.
On that day, HOLY TO THE LORD will be inscribed even on the bells of the horses, and the pots in the house of the LORD will be holy like the sprinkling bowls before the altar.

Indeed, every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts, and all who sacrifice will come and take some of them to boil their offerings. And on that day there will no longer be a trader in the house of the LORD of Hosts.
